newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - May 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Differences between post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa and colonial government officials are increasing -- and are being reflected in policies, governing style and personnel arrangements. Some senior officials are worried about possible conflicts after the government and Tung's office pull alongside each other with the handover to Chinese rule on July 1.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Two new political parties were set up in Hong Kong on Sunday. Both the Citizens Party and the Social Democratic Front support direct elections for the legislature and post-handover Chief Executive as well as communication with the Chinese government. They also expressed their desire to be part of promised elections in 1998 for the first legislative council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, as the territory will be called after the handover.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Zhou Nan, director of the Hong Kong branch of China's Xinhua news agency, gave a speech to more than 10,000 university students in Beijing urging them to support Tung and stressing the importance of abiding by the Basic Law, Beijing's mini-constitution for the territory.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Hong Kong pop music sector has been influenced by the coming handover, with more political and patriotic songs hitting the charts.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- In the wake of Chinese vice-premier Zhu Rongji's meeting with bosses of red chip companies, Shanghai Industrial Holdings revealed that its parent company and biggest shareholder was considering reducing its stake in the pharmaceutical and tobacco conglomerate.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The soaring share prices of property investment company Pearl Oriental Holdings and timber products manufacturer Pacific Plywood Holdings has attracted the attention of Hong Kong's regulatory authorities.

-- Several investment banks may be preparing to unveil covered warrants in Hong Kong on individual Taiwan stocks despite a recent controversy over the launch of two call warrants in the territory linked to Taiwan's benchmark Weighted Index.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A semi-official representative organisation to coordinate Taiwan's operations in Hong Kong might also serve as an informal channel to communicate with Beijing.
-- A financial expert said that only certain sectors in Hong Kong would benefit from a Chinese interest rate cut, reflecting the uneven integration between the two economies.
